summary: # CLO Skills Mini Class: Adjusting the Strap Through the Cross Buckle ## Introduction Hello everyone! In this technique teaching class, I will introduce you to how to make a strap that can be worn throughout the day. I believe that when you are making 3D clothing, you may encounter styles that need to have the strap added. For example, the shoulder strap of a belt skirt, the shoulder strap of underwear, and the belt of clothing. ## Example: Underwear Shoulder Strap Let's take this underwear as an example. In the shoulder strap part of the underwear, we usually use a 日字扣 (cross buckle) to create an adjustment buckle. We can see that the right side of this underwear showcases the adjustment buckle effect that has already been done, while the left side displays a shoulder strap effect that is sewn directly. ### Creating the 日字扣 Effect So, how do we make a real 日字扣 effect on the shoulder strap on the right side? We can use the attached model to achieve this. There is a mutual effect between the shoulder strap and the accessory, allowing us to create a realistic effect of the shoulder strap wearing the 日字扣. The current accessory model can only be used in CPU simulation, so we need to switch to CPU simulation here. Then, we can take the shoulder strap on the left and also create a wearing 日字扣 effect. ## Steps to Adjust the Shoulder Strap 1. **Twist the Shoulder Strap**: First, we need to delete the sewing line between the shoulder strap. Then, use the hook and loop tool to hook the shoulder strap. 2. **Adjust the Fabric**: At the same time, we need to adjust the fabric of this shoulder strap, as well as its example shoulder strap and the conflict thickness. After adjusting the numbers, you can add this shoulder strap to the sewing line. 3. **3D Window Interaction**: In the 3D window, click the right button to add it to the inside. By switching the view, you can see the current version of this shoulder strap after adding it to the inside. 4. **Simulation Setup**: To prevent misalignment of the shoulder strap during the simulation process, you can add a row of fixed needles on one side of the board. Switch the tool to the fixed needle and add a row of fixed needles to the double-sided mouse in the center of the outside of the board. 5. **Add a Ring Component**: We can find the corresponding ring component in the close library. You can also choose the component type in Connect and enter the component name to search. Here, we can copy the existing ring component in the current project file and drag it into the 3D window. 6. **Position the Component**: Select the component and use the symbol in the upper right corner to arrange it near the position of the ring. Then, use the positioning ball to move the component to the other side. ## Completing the Ring Effect To ensure the current board passes through the ring, select the grid comparison tool to select all the grids on the back of the small board and use the positioning ball to move it forward, towards the direction of the screen. View it from the side to see the effect of the ring. Due to the copy simulation, the copy is interactive between the board, so if there is a cross between the board and the copy, you can use the selection grid tool to select the area of the surface and drag it out. After opening the simulation, we can see that the current ring effect is also made. ### Shoulder Strap Twist Next, we will make the twist of the shoulder strap. First, turn on the simulation and bring the shoulder strap board close to the ring component using the fixed needle movement. After turning off the simulation, we can create the shoulder strap twist board. 1. **Select and Adjust**: Use the selection grid tool to take the shoulder strap twist board out. Apply the shoulder strap fabric and adjust its particle diameter and conflict thickness. 2. **Add to the Inside**: Increase the sewing line and add it to the inside. You can see that the board has been added to the interior. 3. **Position Adjustments**: Use the positioning ball to adjust the board inside, making it pass through the circular board. Delete the fixed needle here. 4. **Simulation Stability**: Since the shoulder strap board is flexible, we can freeze this ring and adjust its conflict thickness on the right side of the attribute editor, for example, changing it to 0.5. This will reduce the gap between the boards. ## Finalizing the Shoulder Strap 1. **Simulation Check**: Turn on the simulation to check if the board has passed. If it has not, select this part of the grid and drag it out. 2. **Creating the Shoulder Belt**: Now, we will work on the effect of the shoulder belt. To do this, we can create a small part of the pass. 3. **Increase Internal Lines**: On the left and right sides of this internal line, increase two internal lines to position the pass board. Select the internal line, click the right button, and add a 5 mm internal line on both sides. This is also the width of the pass board part. 4. **Adjust Fabric and Thickness**: After confirming, use the selection grid tool to select these lines, then click the right button to select them as a board. Adjust the fabric of the board and its particle diameter, as well as the thickness conflict. Sew this board to the inside of the shoulder belt. 5. **Final Adjustments**: If the current board's center is not passing through the 日字扣, we need to adjust it again. Use the selection grid tool to select the grid in the middle of the board, then push it in. We can also merge the boards into a complete one. 6. **Final Simulation**: Turn on the simulation and check the buckle effect. If necessary, delete one of the sewing lines to create a complete shoulder belt. ## Conclusion This concludes the demonstration on how to adjust the strap through the cross buckle. If you encounter any issues with the simulation, you can use the Select Browse tool to adjust the position, and click on the 3D window to locate it. Then select the blocked part and adjust its position in the 3D window. Thank you for following along!
